newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND BANK INFLATION OUTLOOK SOOTHING - ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND BANK INFLATION OUTLOOK SOOTHING - ANALYSTS.

text.p: The central bank's forecast on Wednesday that inflation would remain well in its target range this year eased discomfort on financial markets where there had been some fears of a pre-emptive rate hike, analysts said.
"In this way (the Bank of Finland) wanted to calm rate hike speculation, said Esko Torsti, chief economist at S-E Banken in Helsinki.
The Bank of Finland said that core inflation which it tracks looked set to remain "clearly within range of the approximate two percent target", despite strong economic growth.
It last raised its key tender rate in June 1995, after which it has cut it in steps to stand on par with the German repo rate at 3.00 percent since October last year.
Money market instruments reacted positively to the central bank statement, with the March FRA rate down 10 basis points at 3.99 percent, and the whole curve some seven to eight basis points lower.
Analysts said pre-emptive monetary policy tightening now would only damage the healthy growth outlook.
"If the Bank of Finland were to react pre-emptively, it would endanger growth prospects," Torsti said.
But all uncertainty was not removed, with some fearing that excessive pay rise demands from unions ahead of pay talks this autumn may after all prompt a tender rate hike.
The last hike in June 1995 was such a move.
Analysts shared the central bank's view that there was no immediate danger an overheating economy, although some expressed concern of bottlenecks in some sectors.

"It is sort of a paranoid situation -- although the unemployment level is currently high, it does not necessarily need to drop dramatically in order to create price pressures," said Juha Lehtonen analyst at Merita Bank.
